To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
brain spectrin interacts with NR2B, and that the interaction is regulated by Ca2+ ions and by phosphorylation of NR2B.
spectrin binds to the N‐methyl D‐aspartate (NMDA) receptor and that the binding is antagonized by calcium and fyn‐dependent phosphorylation.
spectrin interacts with the NR1, NR2A, NR2B subunit of the NMDAR but not with the GluR1 subunit of the AMPA.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the regulation of the interaction of the NMDAR with the actin cyto‐skeleton, a mechanism that is likely to be involved in synaptic plasticity and the morphological changes occurring in neuronal dendrites during synaptic activity.
the molecular basis of the structural and functional plasticity of the postsynaptic density (PSD), which is a complex structure located at the base of the postsynaptically oriented synaptic junction.

the molecular basis for the structural plasticity of neuronal dendrites and synapses, with particular emphasis on the role of the N‐methyl D‐aspartate (NMDA) receptor (NMDAR) and its cytoplasmic binding proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the spectrin‐NMDA‐receptor interaction is regulated by calcium and calmodulins, as well as by phosphorylation.

brain spectrin interacts directly with the NMDA and not with the AMPA receptor, that spectrin binding is regulated by Ca2+/CalM‐dependent phosphorylation of NR2B, and that the spectrin–NMDA receptor interaction may be a mechanism for regulating the actin cytoplasmic cytoskeleton in response to neuronal activity.
spectrin is a novel component of the NMDAR and is regulated in a complex fashion by phosphorylation, Ca2+ and CaM.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
spectrin interacts with the NR2B subunit and this interaction is antagonized by Ca ^{2+} and fyn‐induced NR2B phosphorylations, but not by calmodulin (Ca ^{2+} /CaM) or CaM‐dependent protein kinases.

spectrin is a major actin‐binding protein of the NMDAR and that its binding to the N‐terminal cytoplamsic domain of NR1 is regulated by Ca2+/Calmodulin and Ca2+/calpain, whereas binding to the C‐terminus of NR2 is regulated by CaM and phosphorylation.
the NMDA receptors and the spectrin–actin cytoskeleton are functionally coupled in a manner that depends upon calcium and phosphorylation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the spectrin–NMDAR interactions are regulated by phosphorylation and Ca2+/Ca2+/CaM.

the spectrin‐NR2B interaction is antagonized by calcium ions and fyn‐induced NR2B phosphorylations, while the spectrin‐ NR1 interactions are inhibited by calcium ions and by protein kinase‐mediated NR1 phosphorylations.

the spectrin–NR interactions are regulated in a complex manner by Ca2+, CaM and phosphorylation, which may underlie the role of spectrin in the structural plasticity of dendrites and the actin cytoplasmic skeleton.
